source: Sources: GitHub, HN hiring posts, Stack Overflow, Google Trends

slides.h1: Which programming language is genuinely growing?
slides.p: We checked four signals for 17 languages: code on GitHub, 82,138 job posts, a 10-year developer survey and Google searches.

slides.h2: First: why most rankings are now wrong
slides.p: Stack Overflow questions, Jan–Oct 2026 vs the same months of 2019.
slides.small: Developers ask AI now. Rankings built on questions and searches measure that, not usage.

items: Rust: share of GitHub developers +71%; job posts 6.0% → 8.4%
Python: GitHub share +32%; named in 25% of job posts
slides.p: Shares, not counts: these three are pulling ahead of the rest.
Still used and hired for. Just a smaller share of what is new.

slides.h2: Where the next two years point
items: Rust: +25% vs the average language (84% chance of gaining)
slides.p: A tested lean, not a certainty: back-tested on 2017–2024, it called the direction right 71% of the time.
